In [[quantum mechanics]], '''internal measurement''' refers to the [[Measurement in quantum mechanics|measurement]] of a quantum system by an [[Observer (quantum physics)|observer]] (referred to as an internal observer or endo-observer).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gernert |first=Dieter |date=1998-04-01 |title=Information gain by endo-observers: chances and limitations |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0303264797000828 |journal=Biosystems |volume=46 |issue=1 |pages=73–79 |doi=10.1016/S0303-2647(97)00082-8 |pmid=9648676 |bibcode=1998BiSys..46...73G |issn=0303-2647|url-access=subscription }}</ref>    

A quantum measurement represents the action of a [[Measuring instrument|measuring device]] on a quantum system. When the measuring device is a part of the measured quantum system, the measurement proceeds internally{{Clarification needed|date=August 2024}} in relation to the whole system.   

Internal measurement theory was first introduced by Koichiro Matsuno<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Matsuno|first=K.|date=1985|title=How can quantum mechanics of material evolution be possible?: Symmetry and symmetry-breaking in protobiological evolution|journal=Biosystems|language=en|volume=17|issue=3|pages=179–192|doi=10.1016/0303-2647(85)90073-5|pmid=3995159|bibcode=1985BiSys..17..179M }}</ref> and developed by [[Yukio-Pegio Gunji]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Gunji|first=Y.-P.|date=1995|title=Global logic resulting from disequilibration process|journal=Biosystems|language=en|volume=35|issue=1|pages=33–62|doi=10.1016/0303-2647(94)01480-U|pmid=7772722|bibcode=1995BiSys..35...33G |hdl=2433/84288|hdl-access=free}}</ref> They expanded on the original ideas of [[Robert Rosen (theoretical biologist)|Robert Rosen]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rosen|first=R.|date=1996|title=Biology and the measurement problem|journal=Computers & Chemistry|language=en|volume=20|issue=1|pages=95–100|doi=10.1016/S0097-8485(96)80011-8|pmid=16749183}}</ref> and [[Howard H. Pattee|Howard Pattee]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pattee|first=H. H.|date=2013|title=Epistemic, Evolutionary, and Physical Conditions for Biological Information|journal=Biosemiotics|language=en|volume=6|issue=1|pages=9–31|doi=10.1007/s12304-012-9150-8|s2cid=15030412|issn=1875-1342}}</ref> regarding quantum measurement in living systems viewed as natural internal observers that belong to the same scale of the observed objects.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Andrade|first=E.|date=2000|title=From external to internal measurement: a form theory approach to evolution|journal=Biosystems|language=en|volume=57|issue=1|pages=49–62|doi=10.1016/S0303-2647(00)00082-4|pmid=10963865|bibcode=2000BiSys..57...49A }}</ref> According to Matsuno,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Matsuno|first=K.|date=1995|title=Quantum and biological computation|journal=Biosystems|language=en|volume=35|issue=2–3|pages=209–212|doi=10.1016/0303-2647(94)01516-A|pmid=7488718|bibcode=1995BiSys..35..209M }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Matsuno|first=K.|date=2017|title=From quantum measurement to biology via retrocausality|journal=Progress in Biophysics and Molecular Biology|language=en|volume=131|pages=131–140|doi=10.1016/j.pbiomolbio.2017.06.012|pmid=28647644}}</ref> an internal measurement is accompanied by a redistribution of probabilities that leave them{{Who|date=August 2024}} [[Quantum entanglement|entangled]] in accordance with the [[many-worlds interpretation]] of [[quantum mechanics]] by [[Hugh Everett III|Everett]]. However, this form of quantum entanglement does not survive in an external measurement, in which the mapping to real numbers takes place and the result is revealed in classical spacetime, as the [[Copenhagen interpretation]] suggests. This means that the internal measurement concept unifies the current alternative [[interpretations of quantum mechanics]].   

== Internal measurement and theoretical biology ==
The concept of internal measurement is important for [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|theoretical biology]], as [[Organism|living organisms]] can be regarded as endo-observers having their internal [[Self-reference|self-referential encoding]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Igamberdiev|first=A. U.|date=2004|title=Quantum computation, non-demolition measurements, and reflective control in living systems|journal=Biosystems|language=en|volume=77|issue=1–3|pages=47–56|doi=10.1016/j.biosystems.2004.04.001|pmid=15527945|bibcode=2004BiSys..77...47I }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Igamberdiev|first=A. U.|date=2007|title=Physical limits of computation and emergence of life|journal=Biosystems|language=en|volume=90|issue=2|pages=340–349|doi=10.1016/j.biosystems.2006.09.037|pmid=17095146|bibcode=2007BiSys..90..340I }}</ref>{{Clarification needed|date=August 2024}}  An internal measurement leads to an [[Iteration|iterative]] [[Recursion|recursive]] process which appears as the [[Ontogeny|development]] and [[evolution]] of the system where any solution is destined to be relative.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gunji|first1=Y.-P.|last2=Ito|first2=K.|last3=Kusunoki|first3=Y.|date=1997|title=Formal model of internal measurement: Alternate changing between recursive definition and domain equation|journal=Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena|language=en|volume=110|issue=3–4|pages=289–312|doi=10.1016/S0167-2789(97)00126-7|bibcode=1997PhyD..110..289G}}</ref> The evolutionary increase of complexity becomes possible when the [[Genotype–phenotype distinction|genotype]] emerges as a system distinct from the [[Genotype–phenotype distinction|phenotype]] and [[Embedded system|embedded]] into it, which separates energy-degenerate rate-independent [[Genetic code|genetic]] symbols from the rate-dependent dynamics of construction that they control.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pattee|first=H. H.|date=2001|title=The physics of symbols: bridging the epistemic cut|journal=Biosystems|language=en|volume=60|issue=1–3|pages=5–21|doi=10.1016/S0303-2647(01)00104-6|pmid=11325500|bibcode=2001BiSys..60....5P }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Igamberdiev|first=A. U.|date=2014|title=Time rescaling and pattern formation in biological evolution|journal=Biosystems|language=en|volume=123|pages=19–26|doi=10.1016/j.biosystems.2014.03.002|pmid=24690545|bibcode=2014BiSys.123...19I }}</ref> Evolution in this concept, which is related to [[autopoiesis]], becomes its own cause, a universal property of our world.{{Citation needed|date=August 2024}}  

== Internal measurement and the problem of self ==
The [[self]] can be attributed to the internal quantum state with entangled probabilities. This entanglement can be held for prolonged times in the systems with [[Quantum nondemolition measurement|low dissipation without demolition]].<ref name=":0" /> According to Matsuno,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Matsuno|first=K.|date=2006|title=Forming and maintaining a heat engine for quantum biology|journal=Biosystems|language=en|volume=85|issue=1|pages=23–29|doi=10.1016/j.biosystems.2006.02.002|pmid=16772129|bibcode=2006BiSys..85...23M }}</ref> organisms exploit [[Thermodynamic system|thermodynamic gradients]] by acting as [[Heat engine|heat engines]] to drastically reduce the effective temperature within macromolecular complexes which can potentially provide the maintenance of long-living [[coherent states]] in the [[Microtubule|microtubules]] of [[nervous system]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hameroff|first=S.R.|date=2007|title=The Brain Is Both Neurocomputer and Quantum Computer|journal=Cognitive Science|language=en|volume=31|issue=6|pages=1035–1045|doi=10.1080/03640210701704004|pmid=21635328|doi-access=free}}</ref>  The concept of internal measurement develops the ideas of [[Erwin Schrödinger|Schrödinger]] who suggested in ''[[What Is Life?|"What is life?"]]''<ref>{{Cite book|title=What is life? The physical aspect of the living cell|last=Schrödinger|first=E.|date=1944|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=0511001142|location=Cambridge|oclc=47010639}}</ref> that the nature of the self is quantum mechanical, i.e. the self is attributed to an internal state beyond [[Measurement in quantum mechanics|quantum reduction]], which generates [[Emergence|emergent events]] by applying quantum reduction externally and observing it.
